review_notes:
I read all four declarations in the file. I checked Mathlib's CharacteristicFunction/Basic.lean for existing `charFun` rules about sums or scalar multiples of measures and found none: there is `charFun_zero_measure` but no add, smul or finset-sum lemma. I also looked at every use of this file's lemmas (FilteredClassShell.lean and TwoRootShellDecay.lean) and at the copy of the same lemma in AssemblyPositiveEnergy.lean.

`norm_weighted_sum_sq_le`, `shellEnergy_weighted_sum_le` and `shellEnergy_weighted_sum_uniform` are inequalities, so they are not simp candidates and I make no simp finding about them. The one simp-interface issue is that the measure-linearity rule for `charFun` is stated only in a combined weighted form and has no simp attribute. Users who need the plain sum case have to specialise it to `c := fun _ => 1` and clean up with `simpa`.

Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemmas elaborate, which scalar-coercion form simp would settle on (`c • z` versus `(c : ℝ) • z`), or that downstream `simpa` calls would close unchanged.

findings.excerpt:
charFun (∑ i ∈ s, c i • τ i) r = ∑ i ∈ s, (c i : ℝ) • charFun (τ i) r := by
  simp only [charFun_eq_integral_innerProbChar]
  rw [integral_finsetSum_measure]
findings.problem: The fact that `charFun` is linear in the measure is given only as one bundled pattern, `charFun (∑ i ∈ s, c i • τ i) r`, and it is not tagged `@[simp]`. Neither this file nor Mathlib (pinned version) has atomic rules for `charFun (μ + ν)`, `charFun (c • μ)` or `charFun (∑ i ∈ s, μ i)`. So `simp` cannot push `charFun` through a plain sum of measures. Users with an unweighted sum `charFun (∑ i ∈ F, τ i) r` must instantiate the weighted lemma at `fun _ => 1` and then run `simpa` to remove `one_smul` and `NNReal.coe_one` (FilteredClassShell.lean, line 19). The same lemma was copied as `assembly_charFun_weighted_sum` (AssemblyPositiveEnergy.lean, lines 43–52), and its plain sum case is again recovered through `simpa only [one_smul,NNReal.coe_one]`. The proof here also has to unfold to integrals because no such rules exist.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the bundled lemma with atomic, simp-oriented lemmas that rewrite left to right (the measure-level operation becomes a pointwise operation on ℂ). Each would carry `[IsFiniteMeasure _]` hypotheses for integrability:
`@[simp] lemma charFun_add_measure [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : charFun (μ + ν) t = charFun μ t + charFun ν t`
`@[simp] lemma charFun_smul_measure (c : ℝ≥0) : charFun (c • μ) t = (c : ℝ) • charFun μ t` (proof via `integral_smul_nnreal_measure`)
`@[simp] lemma charFun_finsetSum_measure [∀ i, IsFiniteMeasure (τ i)] : charFun (∑ i ∈ s, τ i) t = ∑ i ∈ s, charFun (τ i) t` (proof via `integral_finsetSum_measure` and `(BoundedContinuousFunction.innerProbChar t).integrable`, as in the current proof).
`charFun_weighted_sum` then becomes `by simp`, or can be dropped. The `he` steps in `positive_shell_finite_sum` and `assemblyPositiveEnergy_sum` become direct `simp` or `rw [charFun_finsetSum_measure]` calls.
findings.benefit: `charFun` applied to any finite mixture of finite measures, weighted or not, gets one simp normal form: a sum of scalar multiples of the component `charFun`s. Users no longer need the `fun _ => 1` specialisation followed by `simpa only [one_smul, NNReal.coe_one]`. Each lemma's left-hand side is a single measure constructor and its right-hand side has strictly smaller `charFun` arguments, so the rewrites terminate and do not compete. The bundled lemma's pattern also only matches a sum whose summands are literally scalar multiples (`c i • τ i`), whereas atomic rules apply to sums, single scalings and binary additions alike.

have he (r : ℝ) : charFun (∑ i ∈ F, τ i) r = ∑ i ∈ F, charFun (τ i) r := by
    simpa using PlanarFalconer.charFun_weighted_sum F (fun _ => (1:ℝ≥0)) τ r

have he (r : ℝ) : charFun (∑ i,τ i) r = ∑ i,charFun (τ i) r := by
    simpa only [one_smul,NNReal.coe_one] using
      assembly_charFun_weighted_sum Finset.univ (fun _ => 1) τ r
lemma charFun_zero_measure : charFun (0 : Measure E) t = 0 := by simp [charFun_apply]
